messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A temporary fix used to expose a fault. the one part you expected to use turns out to be missing. Putting everything back would waste a lot of effort. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "I put the wrong part back. I remove the edge. The fault is still there. I mark the wrong part. I put the repair first. Then the rest. I keep the gap. I keep the repair."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i leave the fault where it is and keep the small piece. i write the date on a loose sketchbook page and keep the missing part in my drawer."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i turn the fault with my thumbnail and the part that still fits disappears. i leave it there, half-expecting the other part to be the one that has been waiting. now i have to decide whether the fault is still hidden somewhere else. i keep the one part and wait for the other one to move."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i leave the fault part where it is and put the temporary fix in a nearby bench. i mark the old part with pencil, then turn it once. if it still catches, i leave the bench and keep the fault part."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I put the faulty part in the sand and pocket the loose bolt. “I put the part I expect in the fault. then I take the bolt and leave the sand in the repair shop. maybe the fault is waiting for the wrong piece.”"}, {"id": "R030", "response": "I mark the scratched edge with grease and leave the old part beside the broken one. I tap twice, then leave the scratched edge alone. I mark the scratch again with grease, leave the old part beside the broken one, and leave the scratched edge alone in place. If the fault stays, I mark the scratch twice again."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i tap the page edge twice, then put the missing part aside and write the fault beside the original. i tap the paper once more, then leave the missing section crooked. the fault looks crookeder now, so i write the missing part on the opposite side."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "I pull the faulty piece out and look at the missing part. “That was easy,” I say. Then I put the faulty piece back and check the other one."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "I turn the faulty part once. The light catches the tooth. I leave it there. The fault has been found. I turn the rest of the place over and leave the door open."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i put the faulty part back on a folded paper strip and mark the fault with grease. i leave the original test mark on the new part, then leave the strip visible and watch where the new part moves. if the fault stays, i keep the old mark and leave the strip unchanged."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "I put the splint over the loose board. \"The fault was wrong. I put the nail back.\" I move the splint closer. \"The edge is still there. I put the iron back where it came.\" I leave the nail in the crack. \"The other part was wrong. I put the weight on the board.\""}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i turn the faulty part and leave it on the bench for a moment. then i test the hinge with my thumb, but leave the old screw seated. i leave the bench still and mark the old screw with chalk."}]
